authority: READ_ONLY_ADVISORY — the reporter measures and prints. Arming any alert on these budgets is an operator decision (AGENTS.md §17).
notes: Targets live here, not in code: scripts/lib/slo_burn_rate.py holds no number an operator would want to change.
Every feed below was verified against information_schema on 2026-09-22 before being written down. No column is assumed.

The four tiers are the Google SRE Workbook multiwindow table. Each long window is exactly 12x its short window, and the same threshold applies to both halves; scripts/lib/slo_burn_rate.py rejects a pair that is not ~12:1.

min_events suppresses a tier whose windows carry too little traffic to make a ratio meaningful. It is per-SLO because a bursty event feed and a fixed-cadence freshness feed have very different sample rates.
tier_table: 1h/5m @14.4 PAGE (2% of budget), 6h/30m @6 PAGE (5%), 24h/2h @3 TICKET (10%), 72h/6h @1 TICKET (10%)

slos.name: alert_delivery
slos.description: An alert is delivered when the row carries a provider message id. SLI = alert_events with telegram_message_id NOT NULL / all alert_events in window.

feed.verified_note: information_schema: alert_events has 26 columns; telegram_message_id (text, nullable) and created_at (timestamptz) both exist. 8,191 rows in 30d, 865 in 24h.
feed.honesty: This measures whether delivery is PROVABLE, not whether a message reached Telegram. Measured 2026-09-22: 11 of 865 rows in 24h carried an id (1.3%). attach_telegram_message_id exists (gate alert_delivery_id, 2026-09-21) but only system_health and data_integrity alerts call it, so the deficit is missing PROVENANCE at the other call sites, not 98.7% dropped messages. Stated as a gap rather than dressed up as delivery failure.
feed.corroborating_feed: communication_events tells the same story independently: 53,038 UNSETTLED vs 79 SETTLED outbound in 30d. Not used as a second SLO because it would restate one finding twice.

slos.name: card_freshness
slos.description: A strategy card is fresh when it was rewritten inside the staleness budget. SLI = 1-minute buckets in the window whose newest watchlist_strategy_cards.updated_at was younger than the budget.

feed.verified_note: information_schema: watchlist_strategy_cards has 22 columns; updated_at (timestamptz, nullable) exists. 5,892 rows; newest 2026-09-22 07:00.
feed.budget_rationale: 36h. A card carrying entry, stop and target older than a day and a half is not something a desk should size a position from.
feed.honesty: Measured 2026-09-22: the producer does not run daily. Distinct update bursts in the last 21 days were 09-22 07:00 (5,430 cards), 09-15 12:00 (13), 09-11 16:00 (72), 09-04 (18) — i.e. roughly weekly. Against a 36h budget this SLO burns hard by construction, which is the finding, not a mis-set target. Raising the budget to hide it would make the number meaningless.

slos.name: quote_freshness
slos.description: Quotes are fresh when a fetch landed inside the staleness budget. SLI = 1-minute buckets in the window whose newest market_quotes.fetched_at was younger than the budget.

feed.verified_note: information_schema: market_quotes has 18 columns; fetched_at (timestamptz, nullable) exists. 777,589 rows over 5,662 symbols after the 2026-09-21 downsample.
feed.budget_rationale: 16h, sized to clear the observed overnight gap (last fetch 09-21 17:00, next 09-22 07:00 = 14.5h) without also clearing a genuine outage.
feed.honesty: No market-hours calendar is applied. The 72h/6h tier therefore spans weekends, when no fetch is expected and none occurs (measured gap 09-19 08:35 -> 09-21 07:00), so that tier reads as burn that an operator would not act on. Tightening the budget requires a session calendar the SLI does not yet have.
feed.downsample_caveat: market_quotes was downsampled 2026-09-21 to 7 days of full intraday plus one close per symbol-day beyond that. Windows longer than 7 days would measure the retention policy rather than the feed; the longest window here is 72h, inside the full-resolution range.
